state.circumstances: You're the general manager of Gordon Ramsay Hell's Kitchen at Caesars Palace. Caesars owns and runs the restaurant under a licence from Gordon Ramsay's company; you run the room, the kitchen and the numbers, and you're paid a salary and a bonus on profit.

setting.name: Caesars Palace, Las Vegas Strip
setting.desc: At the front of Caesars Palace on Las Vegas Boulevard, at the Flamingo Road corner. Tourists who planned the trip around this dinner, fans of the show in pitchfork T-shirts, convention groups and bachelor parties, with a line at the host stand most nights.

ev.text: CES filled every hotel on the Strip, and the private rooms went to tech companies for a week.
Formula 1 race week: the Strip closed to traffic at night. Guests who made it in spent heavily; walk-ins vanished.
New Year's Eve on the Strip: every table booked from five o'clock and a line at the bar all night.
The next step of the Culinary Union contract took effect: raises for every union cook, server and dishwasher.
A new season of Hell's Kitchen premiered, and fans booked tables to see where the winner might end up.
Visitor numbers to Las Vegas dipped again, and the Strip's restaurants felt it on weeknights.
A guest's video complaining about the price of a Beef Wellington went viral. Bookings went up.

log.text: You're the general manager of Gordon Ramsay Hell's Kitchen at Caesars Palace. Caesars owns and runs the restaurant under a licence from Gordon Ramsay's company; you run the room, the kitchen and the numbers, and you're paid a salary and a bonus on profit.

mods.label: Caesars shared services (security, IT, laundry, marketing)

world.notes: This is Gordon Ramsay Hell's Kitchen at Caesars Palace, Las Vegas, the first Hell's Kitchen restaurant, opened in January 2018 on the site of the old Serendipity 3 at the Flamingo Road corner of the Strip. It seats about 300 including a 20-seat chef's table and two private dining rooms, is open daily from 11am to 11:30pm, and is themed on the TV show: a flaming pitchfork at the door and an open kitchen in red and blue. Menu prices are from the current Caesars menu (a three-course dinner prix fixe is $135.95 and lunch $105.95, each built around the Wellington). Caesars runs it under a licence from Gordon Ramsay North America, and Caesars leases the Palace itself from VICI Properties. Sales are the game's estimate: Ramsay said in 2023 it was on track for about $55 million a year, and by then it had served two million guests and 783,000 Beef Wellingtons; an earlier Restaurant Business estimate for pandemic-hit 2021 was about $17 million. Las Vegas visitation fell 7.5% in 2025 to 38.5 million and began to recover in mid-2026. Staff here are Culinary Union members on the 2023-2028 contract. Winners of the TV show have been offered the head chef job here; the staff names in this game are invented, and the licence fee and rent are estimates.

franchise.rules: Caesars, not the player, holds this licence. Gordon Ramsay's company owns the Hell's Kitchen name and recipes and signs off on menu changes; in return it takes a fee on gross sales. The actual Hell's Kitchen contract isn't public: reporting on earlier Ramsay deals with Caesars put the fee at 5 to 6% of sales, with a yearly visit from Ramsay built in.

profile.name: Caesars Entertainment
profile.desc: The company behind Caesars Palace and dozens of other casino resorts across the US. It leases the Caesars Palace buildings from VICI Properties and runs Hell's Kitchen as one of the resort's biggest food-and-beverage outlets.
profile.personality: Big, heavily indebted and run by quarterly numbers. Food and beverage is judged on covers, check and margin, and on whether it fills the hotel and the casino floor. A good outlet is left alone; a weak quarter elsewhere in the company lands on everyone's budget.

rep.name: Dana Kessler
rep.title: Vice president of food & beverage, Caesars Palace
rep.style: Walks the room on Friday nights, knows the cover count before you do, and asks about labour first.

events.text: Caesars Rewards ran a points promotion for dinner at Hell's Kitchen, and the booking sheet filled with loyalty members.
Caesars had a weak quarter across its regional casinos, and every outlet at the Palace was asked to trim spending.

desk.title: A convention group wants the whole room
desk.text: A pharmaceutical conference wants to buy out Hell's Kitchen for a Tuesday dinner: 300 guests, set menu, open bar. Group sales has already told them yes, pending you.

choices.label: Take the buyout
choices.blurb: A very good night, and the regulars' bookings moved.

alcohol.note: Licensed by the state; quotas in some cities.

inspections.system: County or city health department inspections; letter grades posted in some cities.

United States.mealTimes: Lunch around noon to 1pm, dinner from about 6 to 8pm.
United States.customs: Guests expect fast, attentive service, free tap water and refills, and a check brought on request. Tipping 18-22% is expected at table service.
United States.labour: At-will employment in most states; overtime after 40 hours a week; minimum wages set by state and city.
